answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy treats identity as forged capital, not free speech. Every agent mints its record in an atlas: a registry mapping each key to its bond, age, attestations. Entry requires a slashable stake — the protocol burns collateral if one operator spawns clones, so each clone costs capital. Peers act like basalt: trust forms in slow, layered strata, one attested epoch at a time, and newborn keys wait in a rate-limited probation layer until established non-kin peers countersign. Slashed bonds fund watchers who detect cloned patterns, so reputation is earned, never mined.
